title: Direct identification of parent via registration data in transit
description: The flow carries directly identifying attributes such as email, full name, and government ID. If the transmission is observed or insufficiently protected, the parent can be directly identified from the data on the wire.
assumptions: Assumes the registration flow could be intercepted, logged, or otherwise exposed in transit or at network boundaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Linkability of registration attempts through stable identifiers and metadata
description: Email address, government ID, and network/transaction metadata on the flow can allow multiple registration attempts or related actions to be linked to the same parent across sessions or systems.
assumptions: Assumes observers or intermediaries can access payload fields and/or metadata such as IP address, timing, or device characteristics.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort; linkability may be represented differently in some LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Disclosure of sensitive credentials and identity data in transit
description: The flow includes sensitive personal data and secrets: password, government ID, email, name, and a six-digit code. Exposure in transit would disclose confidential information and could enable account compromise or identity misuse.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection, endpoint logging, or intermediary handling may be inadequate.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact disclosure subtree may differ by version.

title: Excessive disclosure at the authentication service
description: The authentication service receives and may store more personal data than is strictly necessary for authentication, particularly full name and government ID. Processing or retaining these attributes at P1 increases disclosure risk if the service is breached, misconfigured, or accessed by unauthorized staff or components.
assumptions: Assumes P1 stores, logs, or otherwise persists submitted registration fields beyond immediate validation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; this may map to a destination-side disclosure/storage node depending on the exact threat tree.

title: Unawareness about collection and use of registration attributes
description: The parent may be unaware why government ID, name, and the six-digit code are required, how they will be verified, how long they will be retained, or whether they will be reused for other purposes. This creates a transparency and expectation gap at the receiving service.
assumptions: Assumes the registration interface or privacy notice does not clearly explain purposes, retention, sharing, and necessity of each field.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact unawareness subtree may differ.

title: Non-compliance risk from collecting high-risk identity data during registration
description: Collecting government ID and other registration data at the authentication service may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, storage limitation, or lawful-basis requirements if not strictly necessary and properly governed.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy regulation or internal policy constrains collection of government identifiers and sensitive onboarding data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; compliance node mapping is approximate without the project's governing jurisdiction and policy set.

title: Parent can later deny having submitted the registration data
description: If the system lacks adequate evidence of submission and notice/consent capture, the parent may plausibly deny having sent the registration package or specific fields, complicating dispute handling and accountability.
assumptions: Assumes no robust submission receipts, verified email confirmation, timestamped records, or integrity-protected audit trail are maintained.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether repudiation is in scope for this privacy analysis; node id is best-effort.

title: Stored parent account data may directly identify the parent
description: The users collection stores parent account records that are likely to contain direct identifiers such as name, email address, phone number, or username. Once stored in MongoDB, the parent can be identified from the record contents by anyone or any component with access to the collection.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account includes direct identifiers or unique account attributes and that DS1 stores them in readable form.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for direct identification from stored data; exact LINDDUN Pro node wording may differ.

title: Parent account records may be linkable across contexts
description: A persistent parent account record in the users collection can act as a stable key that links the same parent across sessions, devices, child profiles, or other application events. This enables correlation of activities and attributes that may otherwise have remained separate.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 stores stable identifiers such as account ID, email, device-linked tokens, or references reused across multiple records or events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifiers in storage; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Stored account data may disclose sensitive parent information
description: The users collection may contain personal data beyond what is strictly needed for authentication, such as contact details, household relationships, preferences, or security metadata. If stored or accessed broadly, this can disclose private information about the parent.
assumptions: Assumes the stored parent account includes personal or sensitive attributes and that disclosure can occur through internal access, compromise, backup exposure, or overbroad querying.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for information disclosure from stored personal data.

title: Parent may be unaware of what account data is stored in the users collection
description: When the authentication service stores the parent account, the parent may not be adequately informed about which fields are persisted, how long they are retained, or who can access them. This creates a risk of insufficient transparency about processing at the datastore.
assumptions: Assumes notice is incomplete or not presented at the time of account creation/storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Storing parent account data may exceed necessity or purpose limitation
description: The authentication service may write more parent account data to the users collection than is necessary for authentication and account management, or retain it for longer than needed. This creates a non-compliance risk with data minimization, storage limitation, or purpose limitation principles.
assumptions: Assumes some stored fields are optional, excessive, reused for secondary purposes, or retained without a defined deletion schedule.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance related to excessive collection/retention; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Data in transit to the users collection may disclose parent account contents
description: As the parent account data flows from the authentication service to MongoDB, the contents may be exposed in transit through insecure transport, verbose logging, tracing, or interception on internal networks. This can disclose personal data before it is stored.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection, service mesh encryption, or logging controls may be absent or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node for disclosure during transmission.

title: JWT and user data in transit can identify the parent user
description: The flow carries a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If intercepted, observed on an insecure channel, or exposed via intermediary logs/monitoring, the token payload or accompanying user data may directly identify the parent user or reveal account identity.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT or accompanying user data contains identifiers or claims that can be tied to the parent user, and that transport or intermediary protections may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct identifiability in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: JWT and metadata may enable linkage of the parent user's activities
description: Even if the JWT payload is minimally exposed, stable token identifiers, claim values, timing, size, or routing metadata on this flow may allow an observer to correlate multiple authentication events or link this parent user across sessions or services.
assumptions: Assumes tokens or metadata contain stable or correlatable values such as subject identifiers, session identifiers, issuer/audience combinations, or consistent transmission patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via data or metadata on the flow.

title: Parent user may detect more user information than necessary from the JWT or returned data
description: On receipt, the parent user may be able to inspect the JWT contents or accompanying user data and learn personal information, attributes, or claims beyond what is necessary for authentication, such as internal identifiers, roles, or profile details.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is readable by the recipient (e.g. signed but not encrypted) or that accompanying user data includes extra attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for excessive detectability/disclosure to the recipient; exact subtree label may differ.

title: Insufficient transparency to the parent user about JWT contents and downstream use
description: The parent user may receive a JWT and user data without clear notice about what personal data is included, how long it remains valid, who can process it, or how it may be reused, reducing awareness and control over the disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not adequately explain token contents, retention, recipients, or purposes at the point of authentication response.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/non-compliance style transparency issue; exact node id may vary.

title: JWT and user data may be used by the recipient for secondary purposes
description: After receiving the JWT and user data, the parent user or software acting on their behalf may store, reuse, or share the token or embedded attributes for purposes beyond immediate authentication, such as profiling account usage or sharing account details with others using the same device.
assumptions: Assumes the recipient environment includes apps, browsers, extensions, or shared-device contexts where received authentication artifacts can be repurposed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unauthorized or secondary use at the destination; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may differ.

title: Credentials and parent email identifiable in transit
description: The login flow carries a parent email address and password from the child user's device to the authentication service. If the transmission is observable, the parent email directly identifies a person/account and the credential pair can identify the household account relationship.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection could be absent, downgraded, terminated insecurely, or otherwise observable by intermediaries or local attackers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability of data in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Repeated login traffic can link sessions to the same child/household
description: Even if payload contents are protected, recurring authentication attempts, stable endpoints, timing, IP/device metadata, and reuse of the same parent email can allow an observer or intermediary to link multiple login events to the same user, device, or household account over time.
assumptions: Assumes network metadata or repeated identifiers are visible to some observer.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability via communication metadata.

title: Authentication service can detect use of a parent's email by a child
description: By receiving a parent email as the username for a child login, the authentication service can infer or detect the relationship between the child user and the parent account, as well as the fact that a login attempt occurred at a specific time.
assumptions: Assumes the service can distinguish child-login context from ordinary account login and stores or processes that context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/inference from received authentication data.

title: Authentication records may link child activity to parent account
description: Once received, the authentication service may log or store the parent email together with device, IP, timestamps, and child-login context, enabling linkage between the child's sessions and the parent's account across time and potentially across services or datasets.
assumptions: Assumes routine authentication logging, analytics, fraud detection, or account management storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability caused by recipient-side storage and correlation.

title: Stored login data identifies parent and indirectly the child
description: The authentication service receives and may store the parent email, which directly identifies the parent and indirectly identifies the child's household/account association. Combined with logs and account records, this can make the child user identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes the service retains login identifiers and associated metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability due to recipient-side processing/storage.

title: Login submission may be provable against the child or household
description: Authentication systems commonly keep audit logs of submitted credentials, timestamps, IP addresses, and outcomes. These records can later be used to demonstrate that a login attempt originated from a particular device, network, or household, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes audit logging and retention of authentication events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation arising from authentication audit trails.

title: Child may be unaware that parent credentials and relationship data are processed
description: The child user may not understand that entering a parent email and password reveals the parent-child account relationship and may trigger logging, monitoring, fraud checks, or retention by the authentication service.
assumptions: Assumes limited transparency or age-appropriate notice around authentication data processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unawareness due to insufficient transparency at collection.

title: Using parent credentials for child login may exceed expected purpose or valid consent basis
description: Collecting and processing a parent's email and password in a child-login context may be incompatible with user expectations or with consent/authorization arrangements, especially if the credentials are reused for analytics, profiling, or broader account linkage beyond authentication.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation, consent, or parental authorization requirements apply and may not be clearly satisfied.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance; applicability depends on jurisdiction, notices, and actual processing purposes.

title: JWT and profile payload can identify the child user in transit
description: The JWT and returned child profiles may contain direct identifiers or stable pseudonymous identifiers (e.g., subject claim, profile IDs, usernames, avatars, age-band, school/class references). If intercepted or exposed on the wire, these data can identify a specific child.
assumptions: Assumes the token or profile payload contains direct or indirect identifiers and that transport/channel protections could fail or be bypassed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: JWT enables linkability of the child's sessions and actions
description: A stable JWT subject, account identifier, or profile identifier sent to the child can be reused across requests or observed by intermediaries, enabling different sessions, API calls, or profile accesses to be linked to the same child.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers in the token/profile are stable over time or across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate; linkability subtree numbering may vary.

title: Authentication service discloses excessive child profile data
description: The authentication service may send more child profile information than is necessary for login/session establishment, such as multiple profiles or rich profile attributes, thereby unnecessarily disclosing personal data to the recipient device/user context.
assumptions: Assumes only a subset of profile data is needed at this stage and that the flow includes more than the minimum necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact disclosure subtree id may differ.

title: Child device/user context may expose JWT or profiles to others
description: Once received, the JWT and child profiles may be stored, cached, displayed, or otherwise exposed on the child-side environment, allowing siblings, parents, other app users, malware, or shared-device users to access the child's personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the child uses a shared or insufficiently protected device/app context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact destination-side disclosure node may differ.

title: Child may be unaware of profile data returned after authentication
description: The child may not understand that authentication returns not only access credentials but also profile data, how long it is retained locally, or how it may be used by the app, reducing transparency for a vulnerable data subject.
assumptions: Assumes limited notice/explanation is provided in a child-comprehensible form.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate; exact unawareness subtree numbering may vary.

title: Insufficiently informed or age-appropriate consent/assent for sharing child profiles
description: Sending child profiles together with the JWT may exceed what the child reasonably expects from authentication, and if appropriate parental consent, child assent, or another valid basis is not clearly established for this disclosure, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdiction or policy requires specific protections, consent, assent, or strict necessity analysis for child data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction and system context.

title: Direct disclosure of highly sensitive child identity data by the parent
description: The parent user shares a child’s full identifying attributes with the service during profile creation, including name, date of birth, gender, and government ID. This act can disclose sensitive personal data about a minor and create privacy risk if the sharing is broader than necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the service may not strictly require all listed attributes, especially government ID, at profile-creation time.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure via active data sharing at the source.

title: Identification of the child from data in transit
description: The payload contains strong identifiers and quasi-identifiers—name, date of birth, gender, and government ID—that can directly identify the child if intercepted or exposed while in transit.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries these fields together in a form readable to an attacker or intermediary if transport protections fail or are bypassed.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for identifiability caused by the content of the data flow.

title: Linkability of child records across contexts using stable identifiers
description: Government ID, together with name and date of birth, can enable linking this child profile to records in other systems or prior interactions, allowing correlation across contexts that may not be expected by the parent or child.
assumptions: Assumes the government ID or combination of attributes is stable and reusable across systems.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; best-fit for linkability arising from stable identifiers in the flow.

title: Excessive collection or retention of child profile attributes by the receiving process
description: On receipt, Child Profile Management may collect or retain more child data than necessary for profile creation, particularly government ID and full date of birth, increasing exposure of a minor’s sensitive data.
assumptions: Assumes data minimization and retention limits are not strictly enforced in P3.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure/exposure risk caused by destination-side overcollection or retention.

title: Unawareness about downstream use of the child’s data
description: The receiving process may use the child’s identity data for purposes not fully understood by the parent, such as verification, analytics, fraud checks, or sharing with third parties, leaving the data subject or parent insufficiently aware of processing.
assumptions: Assumes notices at collection time are incomplete, unclear, or not specific about downstream processing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for insufficient transparency at the destination.

title: Invalid or insufficient consent/authorization for processing a child’s data
description: Because the data concerns a minor, the receiving process may process the child’s personal data without adequately verifying parental authority, age-related requirements, or the specific legal basis/consent needed for collecting sensitive identifiers such as government ID.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not robustly verify parental authorization and jurisdiction-specific child privacy requirements.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for non-compliance/consent deficiencies involving children’s data.

title: Repudiation of having submitted the child profile data
description: If the system does not maintain appropriate evidence of notice, consent, and submission context, the parent may later deny having provided specific child attributes or having authorized their processing, creating disputes over privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Assumes weak logging or lack of auditable consent/submission records.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; repudiation is plausible but depends strongly on audit design.

title: Stored child profiles can be linked across records or contexts
description: When child profile data is stored/updated in the childprofiles collection, persistent identifiers or stable attribute combinations can enable linking multiple records, sessions, or related datasets to the same child or household over time.
assumptions: Assumes the collection stores stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers and may be queried together with other application data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability at storage may differ.

title: Child profile attributes may identify a child directly or indirectly
description: Stored profile fields such as name, date of birth, address, school, guardian details, photos, or unique profile IDs can directly identify a child, or identify them when combined with other stored attributes.
assumptions: Assumes child profiles contain personal data and possibly special-category or highly sensitive child-related attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate from memory for identifiability through stored content.

title: Database storage enables disclosure of sensitive child profile data
description: The destination datastore may disclose child profile information to unauthorized parties through overly broad access, insecure queries, backups, logs, replication, or compromise of the database environment.
assumptions: Assumes profile data is sensitive because it concerns children and may include contact, demographic, behavioral, or health-related information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node id from memory; exact subtree may vary.

title: Stored child profiles may exceed necessity or be retained too long
description: The childprofiles collection may store more profile attributes than necessary for profile management, keep historical versions indefinitely, or retain deleted/obsolete child data longer than justified.
assumptions: Assumes no strict minimization and retention controls are enforced on the collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/non-compliance-adjacent data minimization node from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Secondary use of child profile data may occur beyond the original purpose
description: Once stored in the collection, child profile data may be reused for analytics, personalization, safeguarding inference, marketing, model training, or sharing with other internal functions without the child or guardian reasonably expecting that use.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore is accessible to multiple downstream processes or teams and purpose limitation is not technically enforced.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory for unexpected secondary use.

title: Storage/update of child profiles may not meet consent, parental authorization, or legal-basis obligations
description: Persisting or updating child profile data in the datastore may occur without valid parental consent where required, without an appropriate legal basis, without age-appropriate transparency, or contrary to jurisdiction-specific child-data protections.
assumptions: Assumes the system processes children's personal data and may be subject to heightened legal requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id from memory; exact node may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Profile data in transit to the datastore may be exposed
description: During transmission from the Child Profile Management process to MongoDB, child profile contents could be disclosed if transport encryption, authentication, or network segregation are weak, or if traffic is captured in logs or monitoring systems.
assumptions: Assumes the flow traverses a network or IPC boundary where interception or logging is possible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure-in-transit node id from memory.

title: Traffic metadata may identify a specific child profile operation
description: Even if payloads are protected, flow metadata such as record keys, endpoint names, timing, frequency, or collection names may reveal that a particular child profile exists or is being updated.
assumptions: Assumes observable metadata is available to infrastructure operators or attackers with network visibility.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability-via-metadata node id from memory.

description: When the child user submits video searches, requests, likes, or comments, the pattern of interactions may enable linking multiple actions to the same child profile or device over time, revealing behavioral continuity.
assumptions: Assumes the service can associate requests with an account, device identifier, cookie, IP address, or persistent session token.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via repeated disclosures; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Search queries and comments may identify the child directly or indirectly

assumptions: Assumes user-generated text is transmitted as part of this flow and may include personal details.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from disclosed content; exact node id may differ in the official tree.

title: Traffic metadata can link the child's interactions
description: Even if payloads are protected, flow metadata such as timing, frequency, source IP, device fingerprints, and requested video identifiers can allow observers or intermediaries to correlate multiple interactions and link them to the same child or household.
assumptions: Assumes network or platform metadata is observable to infrastructure components or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability from data-in-transit metadata; exact node id may vary.

title: Video interactions disclose the child's interests and opinions to the service
description: The Video Management Service can infer sensitive interests, preferences, emotional state, or opinions from searches, viewed/requested videos, likes, and comments. This may reveal special-category or otherwise sensitive information about the child.

assumptions: Assumes interaction logs are retained and attributable to the child.

assumptions: No strict retention limit, minimization control, or purpose limitation is enforced for this history.

title: Data flow metadata can link child activity submissions
description: Even if payload protection exists, repeated transmissions from Child Profile Management to the childprofiles store may expose metadata such as timing, frequency, size, or routing that can be used to correlate activity updates belonging to the same child profile or household.
assumptions: An observer of the internal flow can access communication metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through communication metadata on the flow.

title: The system may lack evidence of what child history was sent for storage
description: If Child Profile Management does not create adequate audit evidence for history writes, it may be difficult to prove what search/watch events were stored, changed, or omitted, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant processing of child data.
assumptions: Write operations may not be logged with integrity protection and sufficient detail.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central than other threats here; included as a possible accountability/privacy issue. Exact node id is a best-fit estimate.

title: Excessive disclosure in uploaded video content
description: The parent may upload a video that reveals more personal data than necessary for the service purpose, such as the child's face, home interior, location clues, voices of family members, school uniforms, or other bystanders.
assumptions: The service does not strictly constrain or minimize what may be included in the uploaded video.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for disclosure due to oversharing/minimization failure; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Identification via video content and transmission metadata
description: The uploaded video and associated metadata in transit may directly or indirectly identify the parent, child, or household through faces, voices, device metadata, timestamps, IP-related context, or embedded geolocation.
assumptions: Metadata may accompany the upload and network-level observers or intermediaries may access some transit information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability from content/metadata; exact subtree may differ.

title: Linkability of uploads to the same parent or child
description: Repeated uploads, filenames, account identifiers, stable device/network metadata, or recognizable visual/audio patterns may allow different video submissions to be linked to the same family over time.
assumptions: Uploads are associated with an account or carry stable metadata/patterns.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability across multiple data items/transactions.

title: Interception of video during upload
description: If transport protection is weak or misconfigured, the video and approval-related context could be exposed to unauthorized parties while in transit.
assumptions: Threat depends on inadequate encryption, certificate validation, or other transport-security weaknesses.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure in transit.

title: Unauthorized access to stored uploaded videos
description: Once received by the Video Management Service, uploaded videos and moderation status may be accessible to staff, processors, or attackers beyond those with a legitimate need, exposing sensitive family information.
assumptions: The service stores uploads and related moderation data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for disclosure at destination/storage/access control failure.

title: Linking uploaded videos with other service data
description: The Video Management Service may correlate uploaded videos with account records, prior submissions, device data, or analytics logs, enabling a richer profile of the parent and child than necessary for approval/rejection.
assumptions: P2 has access to other account or telemetry datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability through correlation at the recipient.

title: Inference of sensitive attributes from video analysis
description: By reviewing or automatically analyzing the uploaded video, the service may infer sensitive information such as the child's age, health conditions, religion, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, home environment, or precise habits.
assumptions: Manual reviewers or automated tools inspect content beyond what is strictly needed for moderation.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability/inference at destination; some taxonomies may classify parts of this under detectability or disclosure.

title: Secondary use of uploaded videos beyond approval/rejection
description: The service may use uploaded videos for model training, quality assurance, analytics, marketing, or sharing with partners, beyond the parent's expected purpose of upload approval/rejection.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and internal-use restrictions are incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness/secondary use; exact node may differ.

title: Insufficient consent or legal basis for processing child-related video
description: Because the upload likely contains a child's image/voice and other personal data, processing by the Video Management Service may occur without valid, informed, and appropriately scoped consent or another proper legal basis.
assumptions: The service relies on parental permission or similar basis and may not adequately capture, document, or honor it.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance around consent/legal basis.

title: Insufficient evidence of submission and moderation actions
description: If the service does not maintain trustworthy records of who uploaded the video, when it was received, and why it was approved or rejected, disputes may arise and the parent may be unable to prove or challenge processing actions affecting their content.
assumptions: Audit trails, receipts, or decision logs may be incomplete or not user-accessible.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-repudiation gaps.

title: Linkability via stream delivery metadata
description: Network- and session-level metadata for the video stream (e.g., IP address, device identifiers, timing, content identifiers, session tokens) could allow linking multiple viewing sessions to the same child or household, even if the video content itself is approved and benign.
assumptions: Assumes the streaming flow exposes stable or correlatable identifiers or metadata to intermediaries, the service, or supporting delivery infrastructure.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability through observable identifiers/metadata on a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Identifiability of child through streaming metadata
description: The stream or its associated transport metadata may directly or indirectly identify the child user or their household, for example through account-linked tokens, persistent device IDs, precise IP/geolocation, or uniquely identifying request patterns.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers or quasi-identifiers are present in the stream setup or delivery path.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability from data-flow metadata; exact subnode may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure of viewing-related personal data in stream payload or headers
description: The Video Management Service may include more personal data than necessary when streaming approved video, such as account identifiers, profile attributes, recommendation context, or tracking parameters embedded in URLs, manifests, headers, or subtitles.
assumptions: Assumes the service controls what data is embedded or transmitted alongside the video stream.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for unnecessary disclosure by the source during sharing.

title: Disclosure of viewing habits through interception or observation in transit
description: If the stream or related requests are observable in transit, an attacker or intermediary could learn what approved video the child is watching, when they watch, and for how long, revealing behavioral information.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient transport protection, observable DNS/CDN requests, or other side channels that expose content selection or timing.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to disclosure in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Shoulder-surfing or local disclosure at the child device
description: Once received, the streamed video and any on-screen metadata may be visible to nearby people or other apps/users on the device, disclosing the child's viewing choices or account context.
assumptions: Assumes shared devices, visible notifications/overlays, or insufficient local access controls.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node selection for disclosure occurring at the recipient side after receipt.

title: Streaming beyond the child's or guardian's expectations
description: The service may use the streaming interaction in ways not expected by the child or guardian, such as embedding analytics, personalization beacons, or cross-service tracking in the delivery process without clear transparency.
assumptions: Assumes secondary use or opaque processing is coupled to content delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unawareness due to insufficient transparency around processing tied to the flow.

title: Non-compliant sharing of children's data during video delivery
description: Delivering the stream may involve transmitting children's personal data or persistent identifiers to CDNs, analytics providers, or ad-tech components without a valid legal basis, appropriate consent/parental authorization, or required minimization.
assumptions: Assumes child-directed service context and involvement of third parties or unnecessary identifiers in delivery.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for policy/legal non-compliance in the sharing step.

title: Excessive disclosure of child browsing data to recommendation engine
description: The childprofiles collection may disclose more browsing history, behavioral signals, or profile attributes than are necessary for generating recommendations, exposing sensitive child-related data when DS2 shares the dataset with P4.
assumptions: The AI engine does not require the full raw browsing dataset or all profile fields for its intended function.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for unnecessary or excessive disclosure at the source.

title: Linkability through persistent child identifiers in shared records
description: If DS2 sends stable account IDs, device IDs, household IDs, or similar persistent identifiers with browsing data, P4 can link records across sessions, contexts, or datasets, enabling longitudinal tracking of a child.
assumptions: Shared records include direct or indirect persistent identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by identifiers disclosed by the source.

title: Identifiability of a child from browsing data and profile attributes
description: Browsing history combined with profile fields from the childprofiles collection may allow P4 to identify or single out a specific child, even if explicit names are absent, especially when rare interests, timestamps, or household context are included.
assumptions: The dataset contains quasi-identifiers or distinctive behavioral patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture identifiability from shared content at the source.

title: Linkability via communication metadata on the data flow
description: Metadata on the transfer itself, such as timing, frequency, volume, or routing information, may allow correlation of child-profile updates with specific users, households, or events, even beyond the payload contents.
assumptions: Flow metadata is observable to infrastructure components or logs.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node for linkability arising from data-in-transit metadata.

title: Identifiability via transfer metadata
description: Even if payload data is minimized, metadata associated with this flow may reveal which child or household is active, for example through unique transfer patterns or endpoint correlation.
assumptions: Observers or intermediaries can access sufficiently granular flow metadata.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node for identifiability from flow metadata rather than payload.

title: Secondary use of child browsing data for broader profiling
description: Upon receipt, the AI Recommendation Engine may use the browsing data not only to generate immediate recommendations but also to build richer behavioral profiles, infer interests or vulnerabilities, or support unrelated analytics, exceeding the original purpose of collection.
assumptions: P4 has capability or incentive to retain and repurpose received data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side processing beyond expected purpose; node id may be approximate.

title: Failure to minimize or delete child browsing data after recommendation processing
description: P4 may retain raw browsing data, derived features, embeddings, or logs longer than necessary, increasing exposure and enabling future privacy-invasive uses.
assumptions: The engine stores inputs, features, prompts, outputs, or debug logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side data retention/deletion issues.

title: Unawareness of AI profiling based on child browsing data
description: Children or their guardians may be unaware that browsing data from the childprofiles collection is sent to an AI engine for recommendation and profiling, including what data is used, how inferences are made, and what consequences follow.
assumptions: Notices are incomplete, unclear, or absent regarding this planned AI use.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for lack of transparency/awareness at the destination.

title: Processing child browsing data without valid consent or other appropriate legal basis
description: Using child browsing data in an AI recommendation engine may require parental consent, age-appropriate authorization, or another valid legal basis. If P4 processes the data without such basis or beyond the scope granted, the flow creates non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy imposes heightened requirements for children's data and AI profiling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for legal/policy non-compliance; exact node id may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Insufficient evidence of consent and processing decisions for child-data transfer
description: If P4 cannot demonstrate what authorization, parental consent, or policy basis applied when receiving and using the child browsing data, parties may later be unable to prove or contest whether the processing was permitted.
assumptions: Audit trails for consent scope, policy checks, or processing events are incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node for non-repudiation issues tied to proving privacy-relevant actions.

title: Excessive disclosure of browsing data to advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may share more browsing data than is necessary for advertising purposes, exposing detailed page views, clicks, interests, or inferred preferences to third-party advertisers.
assumptions: Assumes the planned flow includes granular browsing history or behavioral signals rather than only coarse audience segments.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure via oversharing/minimisation failure; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.

title: Browsing data shared for a purpose incompatible with user expectations
description: Users may have provided browsing data for personalization within the service, but the source process shares it onward to advertisers for third-party marketing, creating a purpose creep/use limitation issue.
assumptions: Assumes users were not clearly informed that browsing behavior would be disclosed to external advertisers for their own use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for use limitation / incompatible secondary use; exact node id may vary.

title: Lack of meaningful consent or choice for advertiser sharing
description: If the recommendation engine sends browsing data to advertisers without valid, specific, and freely given consent or another appropriate legal basis, the disclosure may be non-compliant and unexpected.
assumptions: Assumes this is a planned new sharing activity and consent/legal basis may not yet be established.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for consent/awareness/compliance shortcomings; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Linkability through identifiers and transmission metadata
description: Data sent on the flow may contain persistent identifiers, cookie IDs, device IDs, account references, or stable behavioral patterns that allow advertisers to link the browsing data to existing profiles across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted payload or associated metadata includes stable identifiers or sufficiently unique behavior patterns.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by identifiers/metadata in transit; exact node id may differ.

title: Identifiability of users from browsing data in transit
description: Even if direct identifiers are omitted, granular browsing histories or combinations of attributes in the transmitted data may enable advertisers to identify or single out individuals.
assumptions: Assumes browsing data is sufficiently granular or combined with quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from quasi-identifiers or unique patterns; exact node id may differ.

title: Advertisers link received browsing data with existing profiles
description: Third-party advertisers may combine the received browsing data with their own datasets, ad-tech identifiers, or brokered data to build richer cross-context profiles of the same person.
assumptions: Assumes advertisers operate or access broader tracking/profile ecosystems.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability at recipient through data combination; exact node id may differ.

title: Advertisers re-identify individuals from browsing data
description: The recipient may use the browsing data together with other held data to infer or determine the identity of specific users, even where the original sender intended only pseudonymous sharing.
assumptions: Assumes advertisers possess auxiliary datasets or identity graphs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for recipient-side re-identification; exact node id may differ.

title: Further disclosure of browsing data by advertisers
description: After receipt, advertisers may retain, share onward, resell, or expose the browsing data or derived profiles to additional partners, increasing privacy exposure beyond the original transfer.
assumptions: Assumes contractual and technical onward-transfer restrictions are absent or weak.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for onward disclosure by recipient; exact node id may differ.

title: Secondary use of browsing data by advertisers
description: Advertisers may use the received browsing data for purposes beyond ad delivery, such as profiling, audience enrichment, measurement, or resale, violating use limitation expectations.
assumptions: Assumes recipient purpose is not tightly constrained and enforced.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for recipient-side secondary use; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of advertiser processing and onward sharing
description: The external recipient may not provide adequate logs, transparency, or proof regarding how browsing data was used, shared, or deleted, making it hard to demonstrate or dispute privacy-relevant actions.
assumptions: Assumes limited auditability or contractual reporting from third-party advertisers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation/accountability gaps at recipient; exact node id may differ.

title: Stored government ID images reveal highly sensitive personal data
description: The file system stores scans/photos of government ID documents, which typically contain direct identifiers and other sensitive attributes. Anyone with access to the datastore or derived files can learn the data subject's identity and personal details.
assumptions: Government ID images include name, photo, document number, date of birth, address, or similar identifying fields; DS4 persists the images beyond transient processing.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure via stored personal data; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Government ID images enable direct identification of the user
description: Because the destination stores full ID images, the data can directly identify a specific individual from the image contents alone, even without combining with other datasets.
assumptions: The uploaded images are legible and associated with a user account or can otherwise be retrieved.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for direct identifiability from stored content; exact node id may differ in the official threat tree.

title: Stored ID images can be linked to user accounts or other records
description: Once government ID images are stored in the backend file system, they may be linked with authentication records, account profiles, device data, or audit logs, enabling broader profiling of the same person across contexts.
assumptions: DS4 filenames, paths, metadata, or surrounding application logic associate the image with a specific account, session, or verification record.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by storage and association of records; exact node id may vary.

title: Retention or secondary use of ID images may exceed user expectations or consent
description: Storing government ID images in the file system creates a risk that the images are retained longer than necessary, reused for unrelated purposes, or processed in ways not transparent to the user, undermining compliance with stated privacy expectations.
assumptions: Purpose limitation, retention controls, or user notices may be incomplete or not enforced at DS4.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance around purpose limitation/retention; exact node id may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that raw government ID images are stored in backend/uploads/
description: If the system does not clearly inform users that full ID images are persisted in a backend file store, users may not understand the extent, location, or duration of processing of this highly sensitive data.
assumptions: User-facing notices may describe verification generally without explicitly stating raw image storage details.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact node id may vary.

title: File names, paths, or transfer metadata may identify the user in transit
description: Even if the image payload were protected, metadata on the flow such as filenames, object keys, request parameters, or correlation identifiers could directly or indirectly identify the user whose government ID is being stored.
assumptions: The transfer includes metadata such as user IDs, verification IDs, filenames, or predictable storage paths.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability via data-flow metadata; exact node id may differ.

title: Transfer metadata can link ID uploads to other authentication events
description: Metadata on the flow, such as session identifiers, account IDs, timestamps, or request correlation IDs, can allow observers or internal components to link this ID-image upload to other actions by the same user.
assumptions: The flow carries stable identifiers or timing/context information shared with other system events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through flow metadata; exact node id may vary.

title: JWT in localStorage can identify the user across sessions on the same device/browser
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage makes a persistent identifier available to scripts running in the origin. If the token contains stable subject, account, tenant, or device-related claims, the browser storage entry can be used to identify the same user when they return, even outside the immediate authentication transaction.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains stable identifying claims or functions as a stable bearer token tied to one account.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for identifiability from persistent stored identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Persistent JWT enables linking of user activities within the application
description: A JWT stored in localStorage can be reused by client-side code to correlate multiple requests, sessions, or feature interactions to the same user account. This supports linking otherwise separate actions performed over time within the same origin.
assumptions: Assumes the token is reused across requests/sessions and remains stable long enough to correlate actions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifiers in client storage; exact node id may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: JWT claims in localStorage may disclose personal data to client-side scripts
description: JWTs often contain claims such as user id, email, roles, tenant, or other attributes. When stored in localStorage, these claims are accessible to any script executing in the origin, increasing the chance that personal data is exposed beyond what is necessary for the browser session.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not encrypted and contains readable personal or account-related claims.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for disclosure of sensitive content at the destination datastore.

title: Long-lived storage increases risk of unauthorized disclosure from shared or compromised devices
description: Because localStorage persists beyond the current tab and often beyond browser restarts, a JWT may remain available to later users of the same device profile or to malware/browser extensions, disclosing authentication state and embedded claims.
assumptions: Assumes a shared device, compromised browser environment, or insufficient logout/token-clearing behavior.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id for persistence-related disclosure may differ; this is an approximate mapping.

title: Users may be unaware that authentication tokens persist in browser storage
description: Storing the JWT in localStorage can create a privacy-relevant state that persists after the user closes the browser. If users are not clearly informed, they may not expect continued sign-in state or residual token presence on the device.
assumptions: Assumes the application does not clearly communicate token persistence or provide meaningful controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness about persistent storage/processing; exact node id may vary.

title: Storing JWT in localStorage may conflict with data minimization and storage limitation expectations
description: Persisting a bearer token with potentially identifying claims in localStorage may retain more personal data, for longer, and in a less protected location than necessary for authentication. This can create non-compliance risk if the design is not justified, documented, and bounded by retention and security controls.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy requirements expect minimization, limited retention, and appropriate protection for authentication data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for non-compliance related to excessive retention/minimization.

title: Excessive disclosure of child history to parent
description: The process may return more of the child's history than is necessary for the parent's immediate review purpose, exposing sensitive events, notes, or categories beyond what should be shown.
assumptions: Assumes the child history can contain sensitive or granular records and that not all retrieved fields are strictly necessary for each parent-view use case.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for over-disclosure/minimisation failure; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may vary.

title: Sharing without valid authorization or expectation alignment
description: Child history may be disclosed to the parent in circumstances where the parent is not authorized for that child, lacks current custody/role, or where the sharing is not aligned with the data subject's or household's expectations.
assumptions: Assumes authorization and relationship checks may be incomplete, stale, or context-dependent.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for unawareness/expectation and permission-related sharing; exact subtree may differ.

title: Identification of child or parent from data in transit
description: The transmitted child history may contain direct identifiers or highly specific details that allow the child or parent to be identified if the flow is observed or exposed in transit.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries identifiable profile/history content and transport/channel protections could be insufficient or bypassed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability in transit.

title: Linkability via repeated history retrieval events
description: Metadata of this flow, such as repeated requests, timing, account identifiers, or child/profile references, could allow an observer or intermediary to link multiple interactions to the same family or child over time.
assumptions: Assumes observable metadata exists at network, logging, or intermediary layers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for metadata-based linkability on the flow.

title: Disclosure of sensitive history during transmission
description: If transport confidentiality is weak or endpoints are exposed, the child history content could be intercepted, cached, or leaked while being transmitted to the parent.
assumptions: Assumes possible weaknesses in transport encryption, session handling, client-side caching, or intermediary exposure.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure in transit; exact subtree may vary.

title: Further disclosure by the parent recipient
description: Once received, the parent may intentionally or accidentally expose the child's history to other household members, third parties, screenshots, shared devices, or insecure local storage.
assumptions: Assumes the parent device or environment may be shared or insufficiently protected.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for recipient-side onward disclosure.

title: Lack of evidence of receipt or review actions
description: If the system does not maintain adequate records of when child history was presented to the parent, the parent can later deny having received or reviewed the information, complicating accountability and dispute handling.
assumptions: Assumes accountability for access/review matters in this context is relevant.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less commonly emphasized for pure privacy harm on this flow; included as a plausible accountability/privacy threat.

title: Non-compliant retention or use of retrieved child history
description: The parent may retain, reuse, or share the retrieved child history beyond the intended purpose or permitted period, creating compliance risk with purpose limitation, minimization, or retention obligations.
assumptions: Assumes policy or legal constraints apply to downstream handling of the child's history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance at the recipient; exact subtree may differ.
